transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Tech stocks are down sharply as investors' doubts mount over the payoff for massive spending
on artificial intelligence.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq has tumbled more than 3 percent or more than 800 points, driven
by a 30 percent drop in intel, and at one point a 3 percent decline in Amazon shares.
Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, suffered a cyber heist with hackers
stealing more than $6 billion in cryptocurrencies, NPR's Rafael Nam has details.
It's the biggest crypto heist in history, far surpassing the $1.6 billion that was stolen
from a smaller exchange, Bybit, in 2025.
A lot is unknown about how exactly it happened, but so far Binance and researchers that are
looking into this say hackers accessed the trading accounts of customers of the exchange
and effectively stole their cryptocurrencies.
A prominent crypto research firm called TRM said it's highly confident a North Korean
hacking group may be behind the cyber heist.
Binance has promised to cover all losses suffered by customers.
Rafael Nam, NPR News.
The Justice Department has issued grand jury subpoenas to election workers in Los Angeles
County, and PR's Jude Joffe Block reports on what appears to be the Trump administration's
escalation of a feud over California's voter rolls ahead of next week's midterms.
The Los Angeles County registrar recorder's office confirmed it received grand jury subpoenas
last week.
It's unclear at this point whether the employees who were subpoenaed are the targets of the
criminal probe, but federal prosecutors have warned California election officials they
could be committing a crime if they process ballots cast by non-citizens.
The Justice Department is trying to force California to set aside the ballots of people
federal officials say are likely non-citizens.
But a federal judge rejected that request this week.
The Justice Department has appealed.
The same judge also told federal prosecutors to stop threatening local officials.
Jude Joffe Block, NPR News.
These students making up a growing voter block in the elections can find it tough to find
a place to talk politics on polarized campuses, and PR's Janet Ujung Lee reports on an effort
to bridge the gap.
In her first year at the University of Michigan, Sarah Katherine Jackson had a hard time finding
her political home.
I had some ideas that I agreed with the college Republicans.
I had some ideas that I disagreed with them, and I felt like I couldn't voice those disagreements
in that setting.
Same with college Democrats.
I couldn't voice my disagreements with the Democratic Party.
Jackson says the meetings felt like an echo chamber with no room for discussion until
she found a newer political organization called Bridge USA.
They're the tragic assassination of Charlie Kirk.
You have campus violence, and importantly, students are now telling us that we need dialogue
because our lives depend on it.
Janet Ujung Lee bringing us that story.
This is NPR News.
Reaction from inside and outside the Trump administration is reinforcing concerns over
a possible U.S. and Israeli plan to hit Iran again after the midterm elections.
Connecticut's Democratic Senator Chris Murphy says he and other lawmakers were recently
briefed on the possible military plans.
Their plan is insane.
It will lead to devastating escalation and the likely destruction of our commitment to
the rule of law.
Murphy speaking this week at the Middle East Institute in Washington, D.C.
Scottish police say they are investigating how the former Prince Andrew hosted Jeffrey
Epstein at his mother, Queen Elizabeth's Royal Estate in Scotland, and PR's Lauren
Freya reports from London.
The Epstein files released by the U.S. Justice Department include photos of the late sex
offender and his then companion, Ghislaine Maxwell, at the Queen's Balmoral Estate as
guests of her son Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor.
Maxwell is now in prison for sex trafficking, and there are questions about whether any
Epstein victims were trafficked to Balmoral or anywhere else in Scotland.
Police say they've received information but that inquiries are at a very early stage,
with the "needs of victim survivors" at the heart.
This is one of several ongoing investigations related to Andrew's friendship with Epstein.
The King's brother settled a lawsuit with an Epstein victim who says she had sex with
Andrew when she was underage.
He denies wrongdoing but has been stripped of his titles.
Lauren Freya, NPR News, London.
I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News.

Binance suffers over $6 billion cryptocurrency cyber heist, likely tied to North Korean hackers
Justice Department issues grand jury subpoenas to Los Angeles County election workers over voter rolls
